newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee up on Central Bank dlr response.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee up on Central Bank dlr response.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was up slightly against the dollar in early Tuesday morning trade, despite the dollar having made strong gains over major international currencies, dealers said.
At 0445 GMT, the dollar was at 57.60. It opened at 57.65.
The Central Bank, responding to the U.S. currency's strengthening overseas, pushed it up by six local cents and fixed buying and selling rates at 56.5884 and 57.7316.
"Demand (for dollars) is there, but its mostly from the Central Bank rate hike and from the dollar's overseas gains," a Commercial Bank dealer said.
Other dealers said the dollar could drop a few points today as many banks were liquidating their plus positions.
"There is selling pressure. The dollar could come down today," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.
Overnight call money, which opened at 12.5 percent was down to 12.25 percent.

The market is well offered and dealers expect rates to stay low after the Central Bank relaxed monetary policy earlier this month. The bank cut statutory reserves by one percent and allowed exporters to borrow in foreign currency.
